The Government of Vietnam Proposes a Pilot Visa for Remote Workers

Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Lam Thi Phuong Thanh presented a draft resolution on special mechanisms and policies for tourism development to the National Assembly. The draft proposes a controlled pilot program for foreigners working remotely in Vietnam. It also includes more flexible visa and residency conditions for medical tourists and individuals coming for long-term treatment, rehabilitation, or relaxation, along with accompanying family members.

The proposal aims to attract higher-spending tourists and strengthen the competitiveness of the tourism industry. The draft includes the expansion of bilateral visa-free regimes for key markets and a more flexible visa policy prioritizing high-income, long-stay, and repeat visitors, as well as conference participants. The government also proposes simplifying the issuance of work permits, visas, and temporary residence for foreign experts and artists involved in tourism projects.

The pilot program for remote workers has not yet been adopted. The Culture and Social Affairs Committee of the National Assembly, while assessing the project, noted that the resolution should not establish specific visa rules for separate groups and called for further clarification on the novelty, features, and boundaries of the proposed special visa policy. Specific rules, fees, and application procedures for the pilot visa have not been established. Remote workers will continue to use the standard electronic visa valid for up to 90 days.

📌 Token Approvals: Why an Old "Approve" Can Drain Your Wallet Today

Main Points
⏺ Many dApps ask for permission to spend your tokens before you swap or deposit
⏺ By default, that permission is often unlimited and never expires
⏺ This post explains why old approvals are risky and how to clean them up



1️⃣ Core Idea — An approval lets a smart contract move a specific token from your wallet without asking you again.
2️⃣ Why Unlimited — Apps request "infinite" allowances so you don't pay gas for a new approval every time you trade.
3️⃣ Example — You approved a DEX a year ago. The contract gets exploited today, and the attacker uses your old approval to pull your tokens.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — Phishing sites often ask for an approval instead of a transfer, because many users don't read what they sign.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — Approve only the amount you need, review your allowances regularly with a revoke tool, and remove the ones you no longer use.
Final Thoughts

Your wallet balance is only as safe as the permissions you've handed out. A few minutes of cleanup can close doors you forgot were open.

Thousands of Flights Canceled Across the U.S. as FAA Failure Triggers Nationwide Travel Chaos 🛑✈️

А nationwide aviation disruption has exposed serious vulnerabilities in America's air travel infrastructure, leaving thousands of passengers stranded and airlines struggling to restore normal operations.

The crisis began on Friday, November 13, when the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) imposed a nationwide ground stop that halted flights across the United States for more than four hours. The restrictions were lifted at approximately 8:15 p.m. Eastern time.

According to FlightAware data reported by The Washington Post, more than 6,600 flights within, into or out of the United States were canceled on Saturday alone. At least 1,300 additional cancellations were reported early Sunday. 

More than 10,000 flights were delayed or canceled on Saturday, according to USA Today.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the disruption was believed to be connected to maintenance work at a remote FAA facility. A contractor was replacing aging copper telecommunications lines with fiber-optic cables. Officials are investigating whether a faulty router or human error contributed to the failure. The contractor, L3Harris, confirmed that it was cooperating with the investigation.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said he expected airline schedules to recover by Sunday evening. However, the consequences extended beyond canceled flights. Aircraft and crews were left out of position, creating additional operational challenges.
Delta advised customers with flexible travel plans to consider moving their trips to Monday or later.

This was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a computer system failure disrupted pilot alerts.
The incident raises important questions about the reliability of critical aviation systems.

Millions of Americans depend on air travel every week. When the infrastructure supporting those flights fails, the economic and personal consequences can spread across the entire country.
